note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: Nov 9: NZ election — Luxon's coalition holds a paper-thin 67-seat majority (Labour won the party vote 29.36% vs 29.21%); kiwi firmed overnight; official result Nov 27. US: Democrats sweep the midterms — AP called the Senate, NBC/CBS project the House — divided government into 2027 caps the fiscal-expansion path; yields + DXY fell in Asia on the result. UK: Healey's first Budget DELIVERED Oct 28 — headroom £15B in 2029/30 (vs £23.6B March), OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0%. France: Moody's SPARED France (Aa3 affirmed, negative outlook); Fitch cut France's outlook to negative Oct 30 (A+ affirmed; debt to ~124% of GDP by 2028 from 115.7% in 2025, deficit 5.4% in 2026) — both agencies now negative; S&P reviews Nov 27. Nov 5: Canada Budget 2026 tabled ('Masters of Our Destiny'): 2025-26 deficit C$39.3B (vs C$66.9B forecast); annual deficits C$50-60B, under 2% of GDP, over five years. NZ election preliminary count Sat Nov 7: NO clear winner — National 42 seats, Labour 36; National+ACT+NZ First hold 67 seats, a bare majority; Opportunity crosses 5% (5.9%) and enters parliament for the first time; official results Nov 27 after special votes — no government until coalition talks conclude. NZ election: preliminary count complete (99.4%) — Labour won the party vote 29.36% vs National 29.21% (3,650 votes), but National+ACT+NZ First hold 67 of 131 seats; ~399,365 special votes remain, official result Nov 27 — no government until coalition talks conclude. Nov 9 NY close: kiwi +1.56% to $0.5616, strongest major, as the election overhang fades into coalition talks.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: Nov 11 NY close: no US data today — Veterans Day (BLS holiday, bond market closed). The week's remaining prints: UK GDP Thu 1:00am CT (Q3 +0.7% q/q fcst), Japan PPI tonight 5:50pm CT (6.5% y/y fcst), US PPI Fri 7:30am CT (+0.4% m/m fcst).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: Nov 11 NY close: the CPI print digests (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%, third straight +0.3% core); US PPI Fri 7:30am CT (+0.4% m/m fcst) closes the inflation week; Japan PPI tonight 5:50pm CT (6.5% y/y fcst). German CPI final 2.8% y/y confirms the preliminary.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Nov 11 London: DXY to a four-week high (~102.5) as the Dec Fed hike firms — FedWatch 25bp ~85% (Reuters 09:15Z) after 91.9% in Asia, 50bp tail ~9-15%; the hike itself essentially certain. Paulson: CPI “shows that inflationary pressures remain clearly evident”; Logan: “at least two more rate increases, each by 25bp”. Nov 11 NY close: DXY 102.86 (+0.64%), highest since April 2025; Dec Fed hike 25bp ~87% (CME FedWatch via Reuters), 50bp tail ~13%; ECB ~92%, BoJ ~84%, BoE back-to-back ~67% (morning briefing pricing).
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Nov 10: next CFTC cut (Nov 10 positions) due Fri Nov 13 — Veterans Day Wed may shift the release; the Nov 3 cut (released Nov 6) is still the latest scored. Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): euro net short at a 3-yr low (non-commercial -143,894; contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); yen longs at the 98th percentile (contrarian -1); AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes (contrarian +1 each); GBP shorts at the 5th percentile (contrarian +1); CAD read is population-mixed, held neutral. Scores moved: GBP 3->4, JPY -1->-2, AUD 2->3, NZD 3->4. Next CFTC release Fri Nov 6, 2:30pm CT — the 4pm run picks it up. Nov 3 CFTC cut released Fri 2:30pm CT — percentile scoring vs the Oct 27 cut carries to the 2am run; board scores unchanged. Nov 3 CFTC (released Nov 6): EUR net short -157,791 (5th pct of 20y, 11-yr extreme) and JPY net long +102,321 (98th pct) still crowded; GBP's short unwound (+19,593 w/w to -59,821) out of the extreme — GBP positioning score 1 → 0. AUD -129,457 and NZD -60,015 still crowded short; CAD -41,775 after heavy covering (+24,649). Next CFTC cut (Nov 10 data) due later this week.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Nov 11 NY close: dollar extends its CPI gains (DXY ~102.86, highest since April 2025) while US stocks rally (CoreWeave lifts tech) — the dollar's bid is the rate story, not a risk-off flight; VIX ~19.5 (Saxo morning brief).
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Nov 11 NY close: Brent ~$93.94 / WTI ~$88.08 (Reuters, ~11:50 CT) — +2.7%/+2.4% on the day as Iran's security chief says no enriched uranium leaves the country. Gold spot ~$3,983, below $4,000 after Tuesday's -2.6% slide. EIA Nov outlook: Brent near $100 for the rest of 2026 if Middle East supply constraints persist.
tot.title: Terms of trade
